title: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot
summary: Hertfordshire County Council reports that the Robotiz3d ARRES Prevent robot, which uses AI to detect road defects, filled a small number of cracks in a public-road pilot.
account: Hertfordshire and Robotiz3d trialed the ARRES Prevent robot, which uses AI to detect road defects and fill cracks. The first public-road test took place in Potters Bar on 6 March 2024. The pilot reportedly repaired a small number of cracks. The project reports that detection accuracy increased from 66% to 100% in testing. In February 2025 the BBC reported that the council had moved the ARRES Eye scanner into a months-long test on a trial route. That report gives no results on the durability of the robot's repairs. Long-term repair performance, pothole prevention, cost savings, and population safety effects remain unestablished.
purpose: Identify road defects and repair cracks before they develop into larger maintenance problems.
system: Robotiz3d ARRES Eye and ARRES Prevent road-maintenance robot
developer: Robotiz3d, developed in collaboration with the University of Liverpool and Hertfordshire County Council
